title: MATH 05-03 Mastery Challenge: Polygon Diagonals, Reentrant Angles & Quadrilateral Taxonomy

questions.promptText: How many diagonals can be drawn in a regular decagon ($10$-sided polygon)?
questions.explanation:
$\text{Diagonals} = \frac{n(n - 3)}{2} = \frac{10(7)}{2} = 35$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $\frac{10 \times 7}{2} = 35$.

questions.promptText: What is an inward-pointing angle in a concave polygon that measures strictly greater than $180^\circ$ called?
questions.explanation: An interior angle greater than $180^\circ$ in a concave polygon is called a reentrant angle (outward-pointing angles are salient).

questions.promptText: A rhombus has diagonals of length $14\text{ cm}$ and $20\text{ cm}$. Find its area.
questions.explanation:
$A = \frac{1}{2} d_1 d_2 = \frac{1}{2}(14)(20) = 140\text{ cm}^2$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $7 \times 20 = 140\text{ cm}^2$.

questions.promptText: Which quadrilateral is characterized as a CONCAVE polygon with adjacent sides equal in pairs?
questions.explanation: A deltoid is the concave version of a kite, having two pairs of equal adjacent sides and a reentrant angle.

questions.promptText: A trapezoid has parallel bases of $18\text{ m}$ and $26\text{ m}$ and an altitude of $10\text{ m}$. What is its area?
If a polygon has $54$ diagonals, how many sides does it have?
questions.explanation:
$\frac{n(n - 3)}{2} = 54 \implies n(n - 3) = 108 \implies n^2 - 3n - 108 = 0 \implies (n - 12)(n + 9) = 0 \implies n = 12$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $12 \times 9 = 108 \implies n = 12$.

questions.promptText: A parallelogram has adjacent sides of lengths $8\text{ cm}$ and $12\text{ cm}$ with an included angle of $30^\circ$. What is its area?
questions.explanation:
$A = ab \sin \theta = (8)(12)\sin 30^\circ = 96(0.5) = 48\text{ cm}^2$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $96 \times 0.5 = 48\text{ cm}^2$.

questions.promptText: What is another classical mathematical term for a general parallelogram?
questions.explanation: A rhomboid is a parallelogram with unequal adjacent sides and oblique angles.

questions.promptText: How many diagonals can be drawn from a SINGLE vertex of an $n$-sided polygon?
questions.explanation: From any vertex, diagonals cannot be drawn to itself or its two immediate neighbors, leaving $n - 3$ diagonals.

questions.promptText: A kite has an area of $120\text{ cm}^2$ and one diagonal of length $15\text{ cm}$. Find the length of the other diagonal.
questions.explanation:
$A = \frac{1}{2} d_1 d_2 \implies 120 = \frac{1}{2}(15)d_2 \implies 15 d_2 = 240 \implies d_2 = 16\text{ cm}$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $\frac{240}{15} = 16\text{ cm}$.

questions.promptText: If the side length of a rhombus is $a = 6\text{ cm}$ and one of its interior angles is $60^\circ$, find its exact area.
questions.explanation:
$A = a^2 \sin \theta = 6^2 \sin 60^\circ = 36\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 18\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2 \approx 31.177\text{ cm}^2$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $36 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 18\sqrt{3}$.

questions.promptText: In an $n$-sided polygon, the number of diagonals is twice the number of sides. Find $n$.
questions.explanation:
$\frac{n(n - 3)}{2} = 2n \implies n - 3 = 4 \implies n = 7$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $n - 3 = 4 \implies n = 7$.

questions.promptText: What is the median of a trapezoid with bases $b = 14\text{ cm}$ and $B = 22\text{ cm}$?
questions.explanation: The median connecting midpoints of legs is the arithmetic mean of bases: $m = \frac{14 + 22}{2} = 18\text{ cm}$.

questions.promptText: Which statement is FALSE regarding a Rhombus?
questions.choiceA: Its diagonals are equal in length
questions.choiceB: Its diagonals are perpendicular to each other
questions.choiceD: All four sides have equal length
questions.explanation: The diagonals of a rhombus are unequal (unless it is a square). They are, however, perpendicular bisectors of each other.

questions.promptText: A square has a diagonal of length $10\text{ cm}$. What is its area?
questions.explanation:
$A = \frac{1}{2} d^2 = \frac{1}{2}(10^2) = 50\text{ cm}^2$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $\frac{100}{2} = 50\text{ cm}^2$.

questions.promptText: How many total diagonals exist in a regular Hexagon ($n = 6$)?
questions.explanation:
$\text{Diagonals} = \frac{6(3)}{2} = 9$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $3 \times 3 = 9$.

questions.promptText: In a parallelogram $ABCD$, side $AB = 10$, side $BC = 15$, and diagonal $AC = 19$. Find the length of the other diagonal $BD$ using the Parallelogram Law.
If the ratio of the bases of a trapezoid is $3 : 5$, the height is $8\text{ cm}$, and the area is $160\text{ cm}^2$, find the shorter base.
questions.explanation: $\frac{3x + 5x}{2}(8) = 160 \implies 4x(8) = 160 \implies 32x = 160 \implies x = 5$. Shorter base $= 3(5) = 15\text{ cm}$.

questions.promptText: What type of angles are the outward-pointing angles ($< 180^\circ$) of a polygon called?
questions.explanation: Outward-pointing angles measuring less than $180^\circ$ are termed salient angles.

questions.promptText: What is the area of a rhombus whose side is $5\text{ cm}$ and one diagonal is $8\text{ cm}$?
questions.explanation:
Half diagonal $= 4\text{ cm}$. Other half diagonal $= \sqrt{5^2 - 4^2} = 3\text{ cm} \implies d_2 = 6\text{ cm}$. Area $= \frac{1}{2}(8)(6) = 24\text{ cm}^2$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $4 \times 3 \times 2 = 24\text{ cm}^2$.

questions.promptText: How many total non-overlapping internal triangles are created when all diagonals from one vertex of an octagon ($n = 8$) are drawn?
questions.explanation: Number of triangles $= n - 2 = 8 - 2 = 6$.

questions.promptText: Find the area of an isosceles trapezoid with bases $10\text{ cm}$ and $22\text{ cm}$ and non-parallel legs of length $10\text{ cm}$.
questions.explanation:
Base offset on each side $= \frac{22 - 10}{2} = 6\text{ cm}$. Height $h = \sqrt{10^2 - 6^2} = 8\text{ cm}$. Area $= \frac{10 + 22}{2}(8) = 16 \times 8 = 128\text{ cm}^2$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $16 \times 8 = 128\text{ cm}^2$.
